chunks: From him, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, from Ibn Zurārah, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man who performs the dawn prayer as one rakʿah, recites the tashahhud, then leaves and goes away and comes back, and then later remembers that he had only performed one rakʿah. He said: He should add to it one rakʿah.

So there is no contradiction between these two reports and the earlier reports, because the doubt that necessitates repetition is only when he does not remember how much he prayed. But as for one who assumed that he had prayed two rakʿahs and acted upon that, then later remembered and came to know afterward that he had in fact prayed one rakʿah, he is not considered doubtful, and his duty is to complete what he missed so long as he has not turned away from the qiblah. This indicates that.

key_terms.ٱلشَّكَّ: doubt or uncertainty regarding the prayer

ai.seo_question: If someone realizes after finishing salat al-ghadāh that he prayed only one rakʿah, should he repeat the prayer or complete it?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal ruling concerning doubt and certainty in salat, specifically in the dawn prayer. It distinguishes between genuine uncertainty that requires repeating the prayer and a later realization of an omitted rakʿah, in which case the worshipper completes the missing rakʿah if he has not yet turned away from the qiblah.
